sections.h2: Where and how do I file a deed in Mio?
sections.html:
Oscoda County has one office for both the Clerk and the Register of Deeds. It works out of the Government Administration Building at 311 South Morenci Avenue in downtown Mio, MI 48647. Phone 989-826-1110, fax 989-826-1136, or email countyclerk@oscodacountymi.com. Mailed items go to PO Box 399.

Doors are open on weekdays from half past eight until half past four, with a break at noon for an hour, and the office shuts on most federal holidays. Walk-ins are fine. Documents arrive in three ways:

  • Over the counter in Mio.
  • By regular mail to the box, with a stamped return envelope so the original comes home.
  • By courier, UPS or FedEx, to the street address.

Title agents based elsewhere can send files through CSC Ingeo, EPN (E-Recording Partners) or Simplifile. Certified court documents and death certificates cannot go that route, so ask first.

sections.h2: What fees apply at the Oscoda County register?
sections.html:
The county's Register of Deeds page lists no prices, so the numbers below are the state's schedule in MCL 600.2567. Phone 989-826-1110 for the exact total, including any card or vendor surcharge, before a check goes in the mail.

State fee schedule for registers of deeds, MCL 600.2567(1), Michigan Legislature
ServiceFee
Entering and recording a document of any length$30.00
Each added instrument released or assigned by the same paper$3.00
Copy of a record$1.00 a page
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00
Name search by staff50 cents a year, $5.00 minimum

The county's page also says copies must be taken in paper form, and phone photos of records are not allowed.

sections.h2: What transfer tax does a Mio-area sale pay?
sections.html:
Two taxes ride on every deed. The state charges $3.75 per $500 of price (MCL 207.525), and the county charges 55 cents per $500 (MCL 207.504). A part-block rounds up. The price must be shown on the deed itself or in an attached affidavit.

Picture a $125,000 sale, near the $125,500 middle home value the Census Bureau lists for Oscoda County. That is 250 blocks. The state portion is $937.50, the county portion is $137.50, and $1,075 is due together. A $60,000 cabin lands at $516.

Exemptions the two laws share, and one they do not:

  • Price under $100.
  • Transfers ordered by a court with no price attached.
  • Boundary straightening with no money paid.
  • Quitclaims that only repair a flaw in title already held.
  • Family deeds from parent to child or grandchild, which excuse the state tax and nothing more.

Put the exemption in writing on the deed.

sections.h2: What do the Oscoda County land records offer owners?
sections.html:
The archive reaches into the late 1800s. Anything from 1985 forward is electronic, and older material is on microfiche. New filings show up online within five days. Each one is time stamped, checked, numbered, indexed and scanned.

Searches go by the property owner's name, and several public computers sit in the office. The staff do not run title searches. They send people to a title company or a private searcher. The county's view is that ownership follows whatever documents the office has recorded, so a seller with an old unrecorded deed in a drawer should file it before listing.

Online tools come in three flavors. Fidlar Laredo is a subscription program with a software download, popular for heavy searching. Fidlar Tapestry bills as you go and spans several Michigan counties. A free direct search link also exists on the county page.

Property Fraud Alert costs county landowners nothing and starts at 1-800-728-3858 or propertyfraudalert.com/mioscoda. It alerts you right away when a paper is recorded against your parcel. The county page adds that the Youngblood Law, House Bills 5598 and 5599, signed in November 2024, makes filing a fraudulent document with any Michigan register of deeds a felony.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Mio office accepts it?
sections.html:
The office drafts nothing and keeps no legal forms. It recommends an attorney or title company, and for do-it-yourselfers it names MichiganLegalHelp.org and eforms.com as starting places. Staff cannot say how a deed should be prepared.

MCL 565.201 governs the page itself: dark ink signatures with printed names, the grantee's address, the drafter's name and address, and a 2.5 inch clear top margin on the first page. MCL 211.135 governs tax proof. Before a warranty deed records, the county treasurer certifies that no liens or tax titles are held and that five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim without warranty covenants is excused. Get the certificate from the Oscoda County Treasurer and carry it with the deed to Mio.

sections.h2: What is selling a house in Oscoda County like?
sections.html:
Oscoda County is the only county in Michigan with no incorporated city or village. Mio, the seat, is a census-designated place in the Au Sable River valley, where M-33 and M-72 meet. The south half lies in the Huron National Forest, much of it on the Grayling outwash plain of sandy ridges, jack pine and hardwoods. Neighbors include Montmorency, Alpena, Alcona, Iosco, Ogemaw, Roscommon, Crawford and Otsego counties. The legislature created the county in 1840 and its government formed in 1881. The name is a Schoolcraft coinage thought to mean pebbly prairie.

The 2020 census counted 8,219 people, the fewest of any Lower Peninsula county. The Bureau estimates 8,723 for July 2025, up 6.1% from 2020. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a middle home value of $125,500, owner occupancy of 87.2%, and monthly rent of $681. Household income is $49,515, and about one in three residents is 65 or older. Only 44.1% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and the average commute is 29.1 minutes.

Housing units total 7,792 against 3,788 households, which shows how many homes sit empty or are used seasonally. The Bureau tallied 24 building permits in 2025. Before listing a cabin or woodland home, search the owner's name at the register and ask the county treasurer for the tax certificate, since both steps affect closing speed.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Oscoda County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 311 South Morenci Avenue, Mio, MI 48647. Letters go to PO Box 399 and the main number is 989-826-1110.

faqs.q: Does Oscoda County take deeds by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the original to the PO Box, or ship by UPS or FedEx to the street address, and include a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return.

faqs.q: Which e-recording vendors does Oscoda County use?
faqs.a: CSC Ingeo, EPN and Simplifile. Certified court documents and death certificates are excluded, so call before sending one.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a $100,000 Oscoda County sale?
faqs.a: It is $860: $750 for the state and $110 for the county, if no exemption fits.

faqs.q: Will the Oscoda County office search my title?
faqs.a: No. It is a recording office and refers people to title companies or private searchers, though you may search names yourself in the office or online.
